name: Assegno Unico Universale - SIA Project 24 25
description: The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. The system validates fiscal codes, handles ISEE information, calculates payments, and allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications. Suspended applications may require additional documents. Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.
rawDescription: The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. The system validates fiscal codes, handles ISEE information, calculates payments, and allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications. Suspended applications may require additional documents. Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.
highLevelGoals: To successfully apply for the Assegno Unico Universale benefit for their dependent children.
To have the flexibility to create, save, resume, and update their AUU benefit applications at their convenience.
To access comprehensive information about the AUU benefit and estimate potential allowance amounts.
To track the progress and status of their submitted AUU benefit applications.
To effectively review, approve, reject, or suspend AUU applications to ensure timely benefit decisions.
To verify the validity of applicant data and ensure correct benefit calculations according to regulations.
To handle applications requiring additional documentation or special attention.
To contribute to and finalize an AUU application initiated by another parent.
To modify how the AUU benefit is distributed among eligible parties.
lowLevelGoals: Applicant sends a request to the system to start a new AUU benefit application.
Applicant inputs and submits their personal identification details (e.g., tax code, name, surname) to the system for the application.
Applicant inputs and submits the required details for each dependent child (e.g., name, date of birth, tax code) to the system.
Applicant inputs or links their ISEE declaration details to the application in the system.
Applicant selects and submits their preferred method for receiving the benefit (e.g., bank transfer, postal order) to the system.
Applicant requests and views a comprehensive summary of all entered application data before final submission.
Applicant sends a request to the system to formally submit their completed AUU benefit application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to save the current state of an incomplete AUU application as a draft.
Applicant sends a request to the system to retrieve and load a previously saved draft of an AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to modify data within a specific section of a draft AUU application.
Applicant inputs and submits details for a new dependent child to be added to an existing (draft or submitted) AUU application.
Applicant uploads specific additional documents to the system in response to a request for more information for a suspended AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to permanently remove a saved draft of an AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to access general descriptive information about the AUU benefit.
Applicant inputs specific family income and composition data into the system to calculate an estimated benefit amount.
Applicant sends a request to the system to display the calculated estimated AUU allowance amount based on provided data.
Applicant sends a request to the system to access detailed rules and conditions for AUU benefit eligibility.
Applicant sends a request to the system to fetch a list of all AUU applications they have previously submitted.
Applicant sends a request to the system to display the current processing status of a particular submitted AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to fetch any notifications or alerts related to their submitted application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to download official documents or communications pertaining to their application.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to fetch a list of all AUU applications awaiting review.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to display all details of a specific AUU application.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to mark a specific AUU application as approved.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to mark a specific AUU application as rejected, providing a mandatory reason.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to suspend a specific AUU application, triggering a request for additional information from the applicant.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to reassign a specific AUU application to another INPS employee for processing.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to verify the applicant's identity against external national databases.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to verify the details of dependent children against external national databases.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to fetch the official ISEE declaration data for an applicant from the relevant national database.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to initiate an automatic calculation of the AUU benefit amount based on verified application data.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to flag an application for manual review due to detected data discrepancies or inconsistencies.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to formally ask an applicant for specific additional documents for their application.
INPS Employee uploads supplementary documents received from an applicant or other sources to a specific application in the system.
INPS Employee adds internal, private notes or comments to an application for tracking special attention or context.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to mark an application's exception status as resolved after all issues have been addressed.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to accept an invitation to collaborate on an existing AUU application initiated by another parent.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to view the details of an AUU application shared with them for collaboration.
Co-parent inputs and submits their personal identification details for the shared application.
Co-parent uploads any documents specifically required from them for the shared application.
Co-parent inputs and submits modifications or completes missing sections within an AUU application shared with them for collaboration.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to confirm their completion and submission of their part of the shared application.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to propose a specific percentage for how the AUU benefit should be distributed.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to view the currently proposed or agreed-upon distribution of the AUU benefit.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to confirm their agreement to the proposed benefit distribution.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to modify the payment method for their specific share of the AUU benefit.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are accurate and cover the main user roles described in the text: the primary applicant, the INPS staff for administrative processing, and the co-parent who can modify or complete applications. There are no obvious omissions or contradictions.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are well-aligned with the system description and actors. They correctly capture the functional needs of the Applicant (applying, managing drafts, understanding benefits, monitoring status), the INPS Employee (processing, compliance, handling exceptions), and the Co-parent (collaborating, modifying distribution). There are no non-functional goals (like security or performance) included, which is correct per the instruction to ensure ONLY functional goals are present. The goals are representative of the core functionalities described.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are comprehensive and well-aligned with the high-level goals and the software description. They correctly capture the functional actions for all three actors (Applicant, INPS Employee, Co-parent). The goals are specific, atomic, and functional. There are no obvious contradictions or major omissions regarding the core functionalities described (application creation, management, processing, collaboration, and simulation). The inclusion of specific actions like "Trigger Automatic Benefit Calculation" and "Verify Applicant Identity" appropriately addresses the system's validation and calculation requirements.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Applicant Successfully Submits AUU Benefit Application
branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process an applicant undertakes to prepare, review, and formally submit an application for an AUU benefit. They cover all necessary steps from initiating the application and providing various required details (personal, dependent, financial, payment method) to reviewing the compiled information and finally submitting the application to the system.

branch_002.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of actions an applicant can perform to create, modify, save, retrieve, and delete their AUU application, including adding details and documents, throughout its lifecycle from initial draft to post-submission updates. They all pertain to the applicant's direct interaction and control over the application's content and state.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Add Dependent Child to Existing Application
Upload Additional Documents for Suspended Application

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Applicant assesses potential AUU benefit entitlement
branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the actions an applicant takes to gather information about the AUU benefit, understand its eligibility rules, and calculate an estimated allowance. These steps are all essential for an applicant to evaluate their potential entitlement to the AUU benefit.

branch_004.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe various ways an applicant can keep track of, check the progress of, and retrieve information and documents pertaining to their previously submitted applications. This holistic view of tracking applications is encapsulated by the high-level goal of monitoring.

branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the various actions an INPS employee performs to review, make decisions on, and manage the workflow of AUU applications. These actions, including listing, viewing details, approving, rejecting, suspending, and reassigning, are all integral steps in the overall processing of applications.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Suspend AUU Application for More Information

branch_006.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the actions an INPS Employee performs to gather, verify, and utilize applicant data from various national databases to calculate the AUU benefit amount, including flagging applications for manual review when discrepancies are found. These operations are all integral steps in the comprehensive processing and initial assessment of an application for the AUU benefit.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Retrieve ISEE Data from National Database

branch_007.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Ensure Application Completeness and Resolve Exceptions
branch_007.rationale: These operations collectively describe the actions an INPS Employee performs to gather all necessary information for an application, document relevant context, and address any identified issues or exceptions, thereby ensuring the application is complete and ready for further processing.

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Co-parent Collaborates on Shared AUU Application
branch_008.rationale: The low-level goals describe a complete workflow for a co-parent to engage with an AUU application initiated by another parent. This includes accepting an invitation, viewing details, providing personal information and documents, making necessary modifications, and finally confirming their contribution to the shared application. All these actions are integral steps for a co-parent to effectively collaborate on and complete their portion of a shared application.

branch_009.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage AUU Benefit Distribution and Payment Arrangements
branch_009.rationale: These operations collectively enable co-parents to propose, view, agree upon, and subsequently manage the practical payment methods for their respective shares of the AUU benefit. They cover the full lifecycle from establishing the distribution to managing its execution.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original goal 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is supported by the project description, which details the process of creating, filling, and submitting applications. However, it is materially over-fragmented relative to the sibling goal 'Manage Application Progress'. The description indicates that creating, saving, resuming, and updating are part of the same continuous workflow leading to submission. 'Manage Application Progress' explicitly covers the flexibility to create, save, resume, and update, which encompasses the preparatory phases of 'Secure AUU Benefit Application'. Since 'Manage Application Progress' is a broader, more accurate umbrella for the applicant's control over the application lifecycle (from initiation to the point of submission readiness), and 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' does not represent an independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome distinct from managing the progress of that same application, it is considered redundant. The submission action is the culmination of the progress management workflow. Destructive-action gate: REMOVE was not unanimous; the HLG is retained in this state. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover the core data entry and submission steps (initiation, identification, child details, ISEE, payment method, review, and submission). However, the project description explicitly states that applicants must 'accept declarations and privacy notices' as part of the application process. This is a mandatory step for a valid submission and is not covered by any of the current LLGs. Additionally, while 'Manage Application Progress' covers saving/resuming, the act of accepting legal/privacy terms is a distinct compliance requirement for the 'Secure' (finalize/submit) goal that is currently missing. Therefore, the decomposition has a material omission.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Manage Application Progress' is supported by the documentation, which explicitly mentions the ability to 'save drafts, resume applications' and 'add children to existing applications'. However, the current hierarchy is fragmented. 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' covers the creation and submission of the initial application, while 'Manage Application Progress' covers the lifecycle management (saving, resuming, updating) of that application. These are distinct stakeholder outcomes: one is about successfully initiating the benefit claim, the other is about the flexibility to manage the application state over time. The reconstruction 'Manage AUU Application by Applicant' is too generic and overlaps significantly with 'Secure AUU Benefit Application'. The original name 'Manage Application Progress' is slightly ambiguous (could be confused with 'Monitor Application Status'), but the description clarifies it refers to the applicant's control over the application's content and state (create, save, resume, update). To improve clarity and distinguish it from 'Monitor Application Status' (which is about tracking INPS decisions) and 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' (which is about the initial successful submission), the goal should be rewritten to focus on the lifecycle management of the application draft and updates, rather than just 'progress'. However, looking at the sibling 'Secure AUU Benefit Application', it already covers 'create applications'. The 'Manage Application Progress' goal covers 'save drafts, resume, update'. These are closely related. Is 'Manage Application Progress' a distinct outcome? Yes, the ability to save and resume is a distinct flexibility requirement. But is it better to merge it? The prompt asks to judge if it should be kept, rewritten, or removed. The original goal is supported. The reconstruction is worse (too generic). The original goal is a valid, distinct capability (lifecycle management vs initial submission vs status monitoring). However, 'Manage Application Progress' is a bit vague. A better name might be 'Manage AUU Application Lifecycle' or 'Manage Application Drafts and Updates'. Let's look at the options. KEEP is possible if the name is acceptable. REWRITE is possible if the name is too vague. The name 'Manage Application Progress' could be confused with 'Monitor Application Status'. The description clarifies it, but the name is the primary identifier. Rewriting it to 'Manage AUU Application Lifecycle' or similar would be clearer. However, the instructions say 'Do not rewrite a supported HLG merely because its LLGs use API-like wording.' The name is not API-like. Is it materially defective? It is somewhat ambiguous. But 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is also a bit action-oriented. Let's consider if it is redundant. 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' includes 'create'. 'Manage Application Progress' includes 'save, resume, update'. These are distinct phases. I will KEEP it, as it is supported and distinct, and the name is acceptable in the context of the description. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Manage Application Progress' is defined as having the flexibility to create, save, resume, and update applications. The current LLGs cover saving (llg_001), retrieving/resuming (llg_002), updating (llg_003), adding children (llg_004), uploading documents for suspended apps (llg_005), and deleting drafts (llg_006). However, the project description explicitly states that applicants can 'create applications'. While 'Update Specific Application Section' implies modification, the initial creation of the application entity (starting a new draft) is a distinct capability from saving an existing one or updating a section. More critically, the description mentions applicants can 'consult submitted applications'. While this might seem like 'Monitor Application Status', the act of viewing the content of a submitted application is part of managing the application's lifecycle and progress from the applicant's perspective, distinct from just tracking status flags. However, looking closer at the sibling HLG 'Monitor Application Status', it covers tracking progress. The most significant gap is the explicit 'create' action. The LLGs assume an application exists to be saved or updated. There is no LLG for 'Initiate New Application' or 'Create Application Draft'. Without this, the 'create' part of the parent HLG is not covered. Additionally, 'Delete Application Draft' (llg_006) is not explicitly mentioned in the project description ('save drafts, resume applications...'). The description does not state that users can delete drafts. It only mentions saving and resuming. Therefore, llg_006 is unsupported. The missing capability is 'Create New Application Draft'.

Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description explicitly states that a co-parent can 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information'. The current HLG 'Collaborative Application Management' covers the completion of the application, and 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' covers the modification of allowance distribution. While these are closely related, they represent distinct functional capabilities (finalizing the application vs. adjusting payment distribution) that are both explicitly supported by the text. No other actor-level functional requirements are left uncovered; all Applicant and INPS Employee responsibilities are mapped to existing HLGs.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' and the reconstructed goal 'Applicant Successfully Submits AUU Benefit Application' both describe the core stakeholder outcome of formally submitting the application. However, the project description indicates that the application process involves creating, specifying details, saving drafts, resuming, accepting declarations, and finally submitting. The sibling HLG 'Manage Application Progress' explicitly covers 'create, save, resume, and update'. The act of 'submitting' is the terminal phase of the application lifecycle. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, if a broader lifecycle management goal exists ('Manage Application Progress'), the specific step of submission is often considered a workflow phase within that lifecycle rather than an independent high-level goal, unless 'submission' has distinct, independent stakeholder value separate from the management of the application state. Here, 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is semantically very close to the final step of 'Manage Application Progress'. However, looking at the hierarchy, 'Manage Application Progress' focuses on the flexibility of creation and updating (drafts), while 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' focuses on the successful completion/submission. These are distinct phases. But is 'Submission' an independent HLG? The description says 'submit applications'. It is a key outcome. Let's look at the redundancy rule. Does 'Manage Application Progress' entail 'Secure AUU Benefit Application'? 'Manage' implies control over the state, including submission. If I can manage the progress, I can submit it. Therefore, 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is likely a fragment of the broader 'Manage Application Progress' intention, or at least heavily overlapping. However, 'Manage Application Progress' description says 'create, save, resume, and update'. It does not explicitly say 'submit'. But 'progress' usually implies moving towards completion. Let's consider the alternative: Is 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' too narrow? It is the final act. The sibling 'Monitor Application Status' is post-submission. 'Understand Benefit Information' is pre-application. 'Manage Application Progress' is pre-submission/during. 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is the transition from draft to submitted. This is a distinct state change. Is it an independent stakeholder outcome? Yes, the applicant wants to *submit* the application. The other goal is to *manage* the draft. These are distinct intentions. One is about the work-in-progress, the other is about the final commitment. Therefore, it is not fully redundant. It is supported. It is appropriately scoped as the finalization step. The reconstruction 'Applicant Successfully Submits AUU Benefit Application' is slightly more precise than 'Secure AUU Benefit Application'. 'Secure' is a bit ambiguous (could mean security or obtaining). 'Submit' is the action. However, the original name 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is acceptable as a high-level goal name for the outcome of obtaining the benefit via the application process. The description 'To successfully apply...' is good. The reconstruction is 'Applicant Successfully Submits...'. The original is 'Secure...'. 'Secure' is a valid verb for obtaining a benefit. I will keep the original as it is supported and distinct from the draft management goal. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover the core data entry and submission steps for a new application (identification, children, ISEE, payment, review, submit). However, the project description explicitly states that applicants must 'accept declarations and privacy notices' as part of the application process. This is a mandatory step for a valid submission and is not covered by any current LLG. Additionally, the description mentions specifying 'household' and 'custody' information, which are distinct from child details and ISEE, and are not explicitly covered by the current LLGs (llg_003 covers children, llg_004 covers ISEE). While 'household' might be partially inferred from ISEE, 'custody' is a specific legal status often required for AUU applications that is not captured. Most critically, the acceptance of declarations/privacy is a distinct, documented requirement for the 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' goal that is missing.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Manage Application Progress' is supported by the description (create, save, resume, update). However, it is a workflow phase (drafting/management) that is a subset of the broader stakeholder outcome 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' (successfully applying). The description presents the application lifecycle as a single end-to-end process for the applicant. Splitting 'managing progress' (drafting) from 'securing the application' (submission/finalization) fragments a single intention. 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is the appropriate umbrella goal that covers the creation, management, and submission of the application. Therefore, 'Manage Application Progress' is redundant and should be removed in favor of the broader goal.

The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. branch_006.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Ensure Application Compliance and Accuracy' is a workflow phase (verification/validation) that is integral to the end-to-end processing of AUU applications. The sibling HLG 'Efficient Application Processing' covers the decision-making aspects (accept, reject, suspend). In the context of INPS employee responsibilities, verifying data validity and calculating benefits are not independently satisfiable stakeholder outcomes separate from the final decision; they are necessary steps to reach that decision. The hierarchy is fragmented by splitting the processing workflow into 'Compliance' and 'Processing'. According to the consolidation audit, when a hierarchy is fragmented and no single sibling yet serves as a valid umbrella for the entire workflow, the broadest suitable goal should be rewritten to encompass the complete intention. Therefore, 'Efficient Application Processing' should be rewritten to include the verification and calculation steps, making 'Ensure Application Compliance and Accuracy' redundant. However, the prompt asks to evaluate the *original* HLG 'Ensure Application Compliance and Accuracy'. Since it is a fragment of the broader processing goal and the sibling 'Efficient Application Processing' is the more natural umbrella for the employee's primary outcome (making a decision), the 'Compliance' goal is a redundant workflow fragment. It should be removed as fully redundant because its capabilities (verifying data, calculating benefits) are prerequisites for the 'Efficient Application Processing' goal, which will be rewritten to cover the full lifecycle. Alternatively, if we view 'Efficient Application Processing' as the umbrella, 'Ensure Application Compliance' is a sub-step. The instruction says: 'Choose REMOVE only when... one named sibling for the same actor already entails every documented capability...'. Does 'Efficient Application Processing' entail 'Ensure Application Compliance'? The description of 'Efficient Application Processing' is 'To effectively review, approve, reject, or suspend...'. 'Review' implies checking compliance. Thus, the compliance goal is fully redundant with the processing goal. The processing goal is the broader stakeholder outcome (timely decisions), while compliance is a means to that end. Therefore, the compliance goal should be removed as fully redundant to the processing goal. Destructive-action gate: REMOVE was not unanimous; the HLG is retained in this state. Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the parent HLG 'Ensure Application Compliance and Accuracy'. missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description explicitly states that a co-parent can 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information'. The current HLG 'Collaborative Application Management' is defined as 'To contribute to and finalize an AUU application initiated by another parent'. This semantically entails both completing the application and modifying the allowance distribution details, as these are the specific actions available to the co-parent to finalize the collaborative process. The previously removed HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' was redundant because its specific outcome (modifying distribution) is a subset of the broader collaborative finalization goal. No other actor-level functional requirements are left uncovered; Applicant and INPS Employee responsibilities are fully covered by their respective current HLGs.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Manage Application Progress' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that applicants can 'create applications... save drafts, resume applications'. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Applicant to Manage AUU Application Content and State' accurately reflects the LLGs (saving, retrieving, modifying, uploading, removing data) and the state transitions (draft, submitted, suspended) involved in this process. While 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' covers the end-to-end submission outcome, 'Manage Application Progress' specifically addresses the iterative, flexible management of the application content and its intermediate states (drafts, resuming, updating) before or during the process. These are distinct stakeholder intentions: one is about successfully submitting a valid application, the other is about the flexibility to manage the application's content and state over time. Therefore, the goal is independently scoped and not fully redundant with 'Secure AUU Benefit Application'. The original name and description are clear and aligned with the reconstructed intent. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Manage Application Progress' is defined by the description 'To have the flexibility to create, save, resume, and update their AUU benefit applications at their convenience.' The project description explicitly supports 'save drafts', 'resume applications', and 'add children to existing applications'. However, the current LLGs contain two significant issues: 1) 'llg_005' (Upload Additional Documents for Suspended Application) is not supported by the parent HLG's scope of 'create, save, resume, and update' for convenience; this action is a reactive response to an INPS employee's suspension request, which falls under the sibling HLG 'Monitor Application Status' (tracking progress/status) or potentially 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' (finalizing the application), but is not a core 'management' action of the application content/state in the sense of the parent's definition. More critically, the parent description explicitly mentions 'create' and 'update', but the LLGs lack a general 'Create New Application' or 'Initialize Application' goal, which is the starting point of 'creating' an application. While 'Save Incomplete Application Draft' implies an application exists, the explicit capability to start/create the application is missing. Additionally, 'llg_006' (Delete Application Draft) is not explicitly mentioned in the project description ('save drafts, resume applications'), and 'delete' is not entailed by 'manage' or 'update'. Therefore, the decomposition includes unsupported actions (delete, upload for suspended) and misses the explicit 'create' capability.

branch_003.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Understand Benefit Information' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information' and 'simulate the expected monthly allowance'. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant to evaluate potential AUU benefit' captures the same intent but is slightly less descriptive regarding the 'information' aspect. However, the original goal is well-scoped, distinct from 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' (which focuses on the submission process) and 'Manage Application Progress' (which focuses on the application object lifecycle). It represents a valid, independent stakeholder outcome: gaining knowledge and estimation before or during the application process. The goal is not redundant with siblings and is not a mere workflow phase of another goal. It is a distinct informational and evaluative capability. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover the two main aspects of the parent goal: accessing general information (llg_001, llg_004) and simulating the allowance (llg_002, llg_003). However, llg_004 ('Retrieve Detailed Eligibility Criteria') is not explicitly supported by the project description. The description states applicants can 'access general AUU information' and 'simulate the expected monthly allowance'. It does not mention accessing 'detailed rules and conditions' or 'eligibility criteria' as a distinct informational capability separate from general information. While eligibility is implied by the simulation, a specific LLG to retrieve detailed criteria is an unsupported addition. The simulation process (llg_002, llg_003) is well-supported by 'simulate the expected monthly allowance'. The general information retrieval (llg_001) is supported by 'access general AUU information'. Therefore, llg_004 should be removed or merged, but as it is a distinct unsupported capability, regeneration is required to remove it.

branch_007.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Collaborative Application Management' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' The bottom-up reconstruction 'Co-parent Collaborates on Shared AUU Application' accurately captures the end-to-end intention of the co-parent to engage with and finalize a shared application. While there is a sibling HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution', it is narrowly scoped to modifying distribution information only. The original HLG encompasses the broader workflow of completing the application (providing personal info, documents, etc.) in addition to distribution modifications. Therefore, the original HLG is not fully redundant with the sibling; it represents the primary collaborative outcome. The original name is slightly generic but the description is precise. The reconstruction is a valid refinement. Given the original is supported and distinct from the narrow sibling, it should be kept, potentially with a minor rewrite for clarity, but KEEP is appropriate as the intention is clear and supported. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain several unsupported capabilities. Specifically, 'Accept Collaboration Invitation' (llg_001) and 'Confirm Co-parent Contribution' (llg_006) describe specific workflow steps (invitations and confirmations) that are not mentioned in the project description. The description states that a co-parent 'can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information,' but does not specify an invitation mechanism or a separate confirmation step distinct from submission/completion. Additionally, 'Upload Co-parent Required Documents' (llg_004) is not explicitly supported; the description mentions that suspended applications may require additional documents (handled by INPS employees/applicants generally), but does not explicitly state that co-parents upload specific documents as part of the collaboration workflow, nor does it distinguish co-parent document uploads from general applicant document uploads. The core supported capabilities are completing the application (providing info) and modifying distribution. The specific LLGs for identification details (llg_003) and updating details (llg_005) are reasonable inferences of 'completing' the application, but the invitation and confirmation steps are invented. Therefore, regeneration is required to remove unsupported workflow steps.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description explicitly states that a co-parent can 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' The current HLG 'Collaborative Application Management' is defined as 'To contribute to and finalize an AUU application initiated by another parent.' This goal semantically entails both the completion of the application (providing missing data) and the modification of allowance distribution, as both are specific actions taken to finalize the shared application. The previously identified HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' is redundant because it describes a specific workflow step (modifying distribution) that is fully contained within the broader intention of collaboratively managing and finalizing the application. No other actor-level functional requirements from the description are left uncovered by the current set of High-Level Goals.

All steps are integral to achieving a successful application submission.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REWRITE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is supported by the project description, which states that applicants can 'create applications... and submit applications.' However, it is materially over-fragmented. The sibling HLG 'Manage Application Progress' explicitly covers the creation, saving, resuming, and updating of applications, which constitutes the bulk of the workflow leading to submission. The original HLG's unique contribution is the final 'submission' step. In requirements engineering, the end-to-end intention of 'applying for a benefit' is a single stakeholder outcome that encompasses drafting, data entry, and submission. Splitting this into 'Manage Progress' (drafting) and 'Secure Application' (submission) creates an artificial fragmentation of a single workflow. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant Successfully Submits AUU Benefit Application' correctly identifies the terminal state of this workflow. To achieve proper hierarchy granularity, the original HLG should be rewritten to serve as the umbrella goal for the entire application creation and submission process, or merged with 'Manage Application Progress'. Given the instruction to choose REWRITE when the hierarchy is fragmented and no sibling is yet a valid umbrella for the *complete* application intention (since 'Manage Application Progress' focuses on the flexibility of progress rather than the final outcome of securing the benefit), rewriting the original HLG to clearly express the end-to-end application submission intention is the most appropriate corrective action. This ensures the LLGs (which cover the complete process from initiation to submission) are properly anchored to a goal that reflects the full stakeholder outcome.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. The system validates fiscal codes, handles ISEE information, calculates payments, and allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications. Suspended applications may require additional documents. Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.

Rewrite the functional intention for actor 'Applicant' using this focus: Express the end-to-end intention of creating, completing, and submitting an AUU benefit application, encompassing the workflow currently split between this goal and 'Manage Application Progress'.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Manage Application Progress' is supported by the project description, which explicitly mentions that applicants can 'create applications... save drafts, resume applications'. However, it is materially over-fragmented. The sibling HLG 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' describes the end-to-end intention of applying for the benefit, which inherently includes the creation, data entry, and submission of the application. 'Manage Application Progress' focuses on the intermediate state management (saving/resuming) which is a sub-capability of the broader application workflow. In requirements engineering, the ability to draft and resume is part of the 'Apply for Benefit' workflow, not a distinct stakeholder outcome independent of the final submission. The hierarchy is fragmented because 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' and 'Manage Application Progress' both operate on the same artifact (the application) and jointly realize the outcome of submitting a valid application. Since 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is the broader, outcome-oriented goal that encompasses the creation and submission, and 'Manage Application Progress' is a workflow phase (drafting/saving) within that same intention, the original HLG is redundant. It does not represent an independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome separate from the act of applying. Therefore, it should be removed as fully redundant to the broader application goal. Destructive-action gate: REMOVE was not unanimous; the HLG is retained in this state. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain material defects. First, 'llg_006' (Delete Application Draft) is unsupported; the project description explicitly lists 'save drafts' and 'resume applications' but does not mention the ability to delete drafts. Second, 'llg_005' (Upload Additional Documents for Suspended Application) is misaligned with the parent HLG 'Manage Application Progress'. The description of the sibling HLG 'Efficiently Process and Adjudicate AUU Applications' explicitly states that it includes 'managing any requests for additional documentation for suspended applications'. Furthermore, uploading documents in response to a suspension is a reactive action to a status change, which aligns more closely with 'Monitor Application Status' or the adjudication workflow, rather than the proactive 'create, save, resume, and update' flexibility described in the parent HLG. Third, 'llg_004' (Add Dependent Child to Existing Application) is partially supported but overlaps significantly with the core application creation/modification capabilities. However, the most critical issue is the inclusion of unsupported and misaligned goals. The parent HLG focuses on the flexibility of managing the application state (drafts, resuming, updating). The essential capabilities are saving, retrieving/resuming, and updating/modifying the application content. The current set includes unsupported deletion and misaligned document upload for suspended cases.

branch_003.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Understand Benefit Information' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.' This represents a distinct stakeholder outcome: evaluating eligibility and potential benefit amounts before or during the application process. It is not redundant with 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' (which focuses on the submission workflow) or 'Monitor Application Status' (which focuses on post-submission tracking). The reconstructed goal 'Applicant assesses potential AUU benefit entitlement' is semantically equivalent to the original but slightly more precise in capturing the evaluative nature of the simulation and information access. However, the original goal is already clear, supported, and appropriately scoped as an independent intention separate from the application submission workflow. There is no material defect requiring a rewrite, and it is not redundant. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the parent HLG 'Understand Benefit Information'. The project description explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information' (covered by llg_001 and llg_004) and 'simulate the expected monthly allowance' (covered by llg_002 and llg_003). The simulation process inherently requires inputting data to generate an estimate, making llg_002 and llg_003 necessary and supported. There are no unsupported LLGs, and no essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG are missing. The decomposition is complete and aligned with the documentation.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. All explicit functional requirements from the project description are covered by the current High-Level Goals. The Applicant's capabilities (creating, saving, resuming, submitting, adding children, consulting status, accessing info, simulating) are fully entailed by 'Secure AUU Benefit Application', 'Manage Application Progress', 'Understand Benefit Information', and 'Monitor Application Status'. The INPS Employee's responsibilities (accept, reject, suspend, handle additional documents) are covered by 'Efficiently Process and Adjudicate AUU Applications'. The Co-parent's specific capability to 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information' is covered by 'Collaborative Application Management'. The retired goals ('Manage Application Exceptions', 'Efficient Application Processing', 'Ensure Application Compliance and Accuracy', 'Flexible Allowance Distribution') do not represent distinct, uncovered outcomes; their functionalities are subsumed by the current, more comprehensive HLGs. No new actor-level goals are missing.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Applicant to Complete and Submit an Assegno Unico Universale (AUU) Application
branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the entire lifecycle of an Assegno Unico Universale (AUU) application from the applicant's perspective. They cover the creation of a new application, the input and modification of all necessary data (personal, dependent, income), the ability to save and resume work on an incomplete application, and finally, the formal acceptance of terms and submission of the completed application. All these operations are essential steps for an applicant to successfully prepare and submit an AUU benefit application.

Add Dependent Child Details to AUU Application
Update Income and Household Information in AUU Application

branch_002.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of actions an applicant can perform to create, modify, save, retrieve, and delete their AUU application, including adding details and documents, throughout its lifecycle from initial draft to post-submission updates. They all pertain to the applicant's direct interaction and control over the application's content and state.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Add Dependent Child to Existing Application

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Applicant to evaluate potential AUU benefit
branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively enable an applicant to gather comprehensive information about the AUU benefit, understand its eligibility criteria, and calculate a personalized estimated allowance. This integrated set of operations supports the applicant in assessing their potential entitlement and the financial implications of the benefit.

branch_004.rationale: These low-level goals collectively enable an applicant to comprehensively monitor and stay informed about the status, progress, and related communications for all their previously submitted AUU applications. They cover retrieving a list of applications, checking individual application status, receiving alerts, and accessing official documents, all of which are essential for tracking.

branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive workflow an INPS Employee follows to review, validate, calculate, and make a final decision (accept, reject, or suspend) on an Assegno Unico Universale application. This includes initial data retrieval and system validation, amount calculation and confirmation, and the management of applications that require additional documentation before a final status can be assigned.

branch_006.rationale: The low-level goals describe a complete workflow for a co-parent to engage with an AUU application initiated by another parent. This includes accepting an invitation, viewing details, providing personal information and documents, making necessary modifications, and finally confirming their contribution to the shared application. All these actions are integral steps for a co-parent to effectively collaborate on and complete their portion of a shared application.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' is supported by the project description, which explicitly details the applicant's ability to create, specify information, save/resume, accept declarations, and submit applications. The bottom-up reconstruction accurately captures this end-to-end workflow. While there is thematic overlap with 'Manage Application Progress' (which covers creation, saving, and resuming), the original goal is distinct because it includes the critical final steps of accepting declarations and submitting the application, which are not fully entailed by the 'Manage Application Progress' sibling. Therefore, it is not fully redundant. The goal is appropriately scoped as an independent stakeholder outcome (successful submission) and aligns with the documented capabilities. The minor difference in phrasing between the original and reconstruction does not warrant a rewrite, as the original is precise and supported. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) provide a complete and accurate decomposition of the High-Level Goal 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit'. Each LLG is explicitly supported by the project description: 'Initiate New AUU Application' (create applications), 'Update Applicant Personal Information' (specify information), 'Add Dependent Child Details' (specify child information), 'Update Income and Household Information' (specify household/ISEE information), 'Save AUU Application as Draft' (save drafts), 'Retrieve Existing AUU Application Draft' (resume applications), 'Accept Declarations for AUU Application' (accept declarations), and 'Submit Finalized AUU Application' (submit applications). There are no unsupported LLGs, and no essential capabilities required by the parent HLG are missing. The decomposition is precise and internally consistent.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Application Progress' is fully redundant with the sibling goal 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit'. The project description indicates that creating, saving, resuming, and updating applications are integral phases of the end-to-end workflow to successfully apply for the benefit. The sibling goal 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' explicitly encompasses the entire workflow from initial creation, specifying information, saving/resuming drafts, accepting declarations, and finalizing submission. Therefore, 'Manage Application Progress' does not represent an independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome distinct from the primary application goal; it is a fragmented view of the same lifecycle. According to the consolidation audit, when a sibling already entails every documented capability and distinctive LLG of the original goal, the original should be removed as fully redundant.

branch_003.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Understand Benefit Information' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.' This represents a distinct stakeholder intention from the transactional goals of applying, managing drafts, or monitoring status. It serves as a pre-application or parallel informational need to evaluate eligibility and financial impact. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant to evaluate potential AUU benefit' is semantically equivalent and well-scoped. It is not redundant with 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' because understanding/simulating is a separate capability from the act of submitting an application. Therefore, the goal should be kept. Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Understand Benefit Information'. The project description explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information' (supported by llg_001 and llg_004) and 'simulate the expected monthly allowance' (supported by llg_002 and llg_003). The simulation process inherently requires inputting data (llg_002) and viewing the result (llg_003). Accessing eligibility criteria (llg_004) is a necessary component of understanding the benefit information to determine if one qualifies for the simulation. missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current High-Level Goals comprehensively cover all explicit functional requirements in the project description. The 'Applicant' goals cover application creation, drafting, submission, status monitoring, and information access. The 'INPS Employee' goal covers processing, adjudication (accept/reject/suspend), and managing suspended applications requiring additional documents. The 'Co-parent' goal covers completing existing applications and modifying allowance distribution. The retired goals (e.g., 'Manage Application Exceptions', 'Flexible Allowance Distribution') are fully entailed by the current 'Efficiently Process and Adjudicate AUU Applications' and 'Collaborative Application Management' goals, respectively. No distinct actor-level outcomes are left uncovered.

branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the entire lifecycle of an Assegno Unico Universale (AUU) application from the applicant's perspective. They cover the creation of a new application, the input and modification of all necessary data (personal, dependent, income), the ability to save and resume work on an incomplete application, and finally, the formal acceptance of terms and submission of the completed application. All these operations are essential steps for an applicant to successfully prepare and submit an AUU benefit application.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' accurately captures the primary end-to-end intention of the Applicant actor: to create, complete, and submit an application for the AUU benefit. The project description explicitly supports this workflow, including creating applications, specifying details, saving/resuming drafts, accepting declarations, and submitting. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Applicant to Complete and Submit an Assegno Unico Universale (AUU) Application' is semantically equivalent to the original goal, confirming the intent. The goal is distinct from 'Monitor Application Status' (post-submission tracking) and 'Understand Benefit Information' (pre-application consultation/simulation). It is not redundant with 'Collaborative Application Management' because that goal is scoped to the Co-parent actor, whereas this goal is scoped to the primary Applicant. The granularity is appropriate for a High-Level Goal, representing the complete lifecycle of initiating and finalizing a new application. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit'. Each LLG corresponds to a specific, documented step in the application workflow: initiating the application (llg_001), inputting personal, child, and income/household data (llg_002, llg_003, llg_004), managing drafts via save and retrieve operations (llg_005, llg_006), accepting required declarations (llg_007), and final submission (llg_008). All these capabilities are explicitly supported by the project description ('create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications'). There are no unsupported LLGs, and no essential capabilities required for the initial application submission are missing. The scope is correctly bounded, excluding post-submission monitoring (sibling HLG) and co-parent collaboration (sibling HLG).

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current High-Level Goals comprehensively cover all explicit functional requirements in the project description. 1) 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' covers the primary applicant workflow, including creating, saving, resuming, and submitting applications, as well as specifying child, household, custody, and payment information. 2) 'Understand Benefit Information' covers accessing general AUU information and simulating expected monthly allowances. 3) 'Monitor Application Status' covers consulting submitted applications and tracking their progress. 4) 'Efficiently Process and Adjudicate AUU Applications' covers the INPS employee's responsibilities to accept, reject, or suspend applications and manage requests for additional documentation for suspended cases. 5) 'Collaborative Application Management' covers the Co-parent's ability to complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. The retired goal 'Manage Application Progress' is fully subsumed by 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' (which explicitly includes saving and resuming drafts) and 'Monitor Application Status'. No explicit actor-level capabilities are left uncovered.

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Applicants to monitor the status and history of their AUU benefit applications.
branch_003.rationale: Both low-level goals contribute to the applicant's ability to stay informed about their submitted AUU benefit applications. One provides an overview list of all applications, while the other allows for detailed tracking of a specific application's status and progress history, thus collectively supporting the monitoring of applications.

branch_005.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Co-parent Collaborates on Shared AUU Application
branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process for a co-parent to engage with and contribute their specific information to an AUU application that has been initiated by another parent and shared with them. This includes accepting the invitation, viewing the application, providing personal details and documents, making necessary modifications, and confirming their part of the submission, all of which are integral to successful collaboration on the shared application.

branch_003.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Monitor Application Status' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that applicants can 'consult submitted applications'. This represents a distinct stakeholder outcome from the initial application workflow ('Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit'), which focuses on creation and submission. Monitoring is a post-submission activity with its own value (tracking progress, status, and history). The bottom-up reconstruction aligns well with this intention. It is not redundant with 'Successfully Apply' because the latter covers the creation/submission phase, while this goal covers the post-submission tracking phase. It is also distinct from 'Understand Benefit Information', which is pre-application informational access. Therefore, the goal is independently scoped and supported. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs correctly decompose the parent goal 'Monitor Application Status'. The project description explicitly states that applicants can 'consult submitted applications'. LLG llg_001 ('Retrieve List of Submitted Applications') supports the ability to see which applications exist, and llg_002 ('View Specific Application Status') supports the ability to track the progress and status of a specific application. Both are directly entailed by the documentation and the parent goal's description ('track the progress and status'). There are no unsupported capabilities (such as notifications or downloads) and no essential missing capabilities for this specific monitoring goal. The decomposition is precise and aligned with the documentation.

branch_005.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Collaborative Application Management' is well-supported by the project description, which explicitly states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' The goal correctly identifies the distinct stakeholder outcome for the Co-parent actor, which is separate from the primary Applicant's workflow of creating and submitting a new application. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Co-parent Collaborates on Shared AUU Application' aligns semantically with the original goal, confirming that the intention is to contribute to and finalize an application initiated by another parent. There are no other sibling goals for the Co-parent actor that would make this goal redundant. The scope is appropriate for a High-Level Goal, covering the end-to-end process of collaboration (viewing, completing, modifying, and finalizing) without being overly fragmented or generic. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description explicitly states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' It does not mention an 'invitation' mechanism, specific 'identification details' separate from the application data, or a distinct 'confirmation' step for the co-parent. LLG llg_001 ('Accept Collaboration Invitation') is unsupported as the documentation does not entail an invitation workflow. LLG llg_003 ('Provide Co-parent Identification Details') is overly specific and potentially redundant with the general application data entry, as the documentation only specifies modifying allowance distribution and completing the application. LLG llg_006 ('Confirm Co-parent Contribution') is unsupported; the documentation states the co-parent can 'complete' the application, which implies finalization, but does not specify a separate confirmation action distinct from the completion/submission process. The essential capability explicitly documented is 'Modify Allowance Distribution Information', which is not explicitly captured as a distinct LLG (llg_005 is generic 'Update Shared Application Details'). Therefore, the decomposition contains unsupported elements and misses the specific documented capability.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current High-Level Goals comprehensively cover all explicit functional requirements in the project description. 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' covers the creation, drafting, and submission workflow. 'Understand Benefit Information' covers accessing general info and simulating allowances. 'Monitor Application Status' covers consulting submitted applications. 'Efficiently Process and Adjudicate AUU Applications' covers INPS employee actions including accepting, rejecting, suspending, and managing additional documents for suspended cases. 'Collaborative Application Management' covers the Co-parent's ability to complete and modify existing applications, including allowance distribution. The requirement for applicants to 'add children to existing applications' is semantically entailed by the ability to manage and update application details within the scope of 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' (which encompasses the entire lifecycle including updates/resumption) or 'Monitor Application Status' (if viewed as managing the active application state), but more accurately, it falls under the general management of the application which is covered by the primary application goal. No distinct actor-level outcome is left uncovered.

branch_005.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Co-parent Manages and Submits Their Contribution to the Shared AUU Application
branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of a co-parent's interaction with a shared AUU application. This includes retrieving its state, uploading necessary documents, updating specific sections, modifying general information, and finally submitting their completed contribution to finalize the application.

Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Collaborative Application Management' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' The bottom-up reconstruction 'Co-parent Manages and Submits Their Contribution to the Shared AUU Application' accurately captures the end-to-end intent of the Co-parent actor, which involves retrieving the shared application, updating specific sections (like allowance distribution), and finalizing their contribution. This goal is distinct from the Applicant's goals because the Co-parent operates on an *existing* application initiated by another party, rather than creating a new one from scratch. It is not redundant with 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit' because the actor and the starting state (existing vs. new) are different. The goal is appropriately scoped as a single stakeholder outcome: contributing to and finalizing the shared application. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs contain unsupported capabilities. Specifically, 'llg_002' (Upload Co-parent Required Documents) and 'llg_004' (Update Shared Application Details) are not explicitly supported by the project description. The description states that the co-parent can 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' It does not explicitly state that the co-parent uploads documents (document upload is generally associated with the applicant or INPS requests for suspended applications) or that they update 'general information' beyond the specific allowance distribution. 'Complete an existing application' implies filling in missing data, but without explicit documentation of which sections the co-parent can edit, assuming general updates and document uploads is an inference not grounded in the text. The only explicitly documented actions for the co-parent are completing the application (which is vague but implies data entry) and modifying allowance distribution. 'llg_001' (View) and 'llg_005' (Submit) are reasonable inferences for 'completing' and 'finalizing' the contribution, but 'llg_002' and 'llg_004' introduce specific CRUD operations (upload, general update) that are not entailed. Therefore, regeneration is required to remove unsupported LLGs and align strictly with the documented 'modify allowance distribution' and 'complete' capabilities.

high_level_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Collaborative Application Management' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' The bottom-up reconstruction 'Co-parent completes and submits a shared AUU application' accurately captures the end-to-end intent of this specific actor. While the Applicant has a goal to 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit', the Co-parent's role is distinct: they are not the primary initiator but are completing and finalizing an application started by someone else. This is a distinct stakeholder outcome (collaborative finalization) that is not fully entailed by the Applicant's goals, as the Applicant's goals focus on their own creation and submission workflow. The Co-parent's goal is not redundant because it involves specific actions (completing existing data, modifying distribution) that are unique to the collaborative context. Therefore, the goal should be kept, though the name could be slightly more precise, but 'Collaborative Application Management' is acceptable and clearly scoped to the Co-parent's specific contribution to the application lifecycle.

low_level_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the Co-parent's role as defined in the project description ('Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information'). 'View Shared Application Details' is a necessary precondition for completing or modifying an existing application. 'Modify Allowance Distribution Information' is explicitly stated in the description. 'Complete Missing Application Data' corresponds to the 'complete an existing application' capability. 'Submit Finalized Application' corresponds to the 'finalize' aspect of the HLG and the general system capability to submit applications. There are no unsupported LLGs and no missing essential capabilities for this specific actor's goal.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The current High-Level Goals comprehensively cover all explicit functional requirements in the project description. The Applicant's capabilities (applying, understanding benefits, monitoring status, adding children) are covered by 'Successfully Apply for AUU Benefit', 'Understand Benefit Information', and 'Monitor Application Status'. The INPS Employee's responsibilities (processing, adjudicating, handling suspended applications/documents) are fully entailed by 'Efficiently Process and Adjudicate AUU Applications'. The Co-parent's specific capabilities (completing existing applications, modifying allowance distribution) are covered by 'Collaborative Application Management'. No distinct actor-level outcomes remain uncovered.
